mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES rebounds from a sharp dip, commuter presence returns first and then lifts nearby retail visits within four weeks. In Tokyo, a one-week recovery in WORKPLACES should translate into higher RETAIL_REC after a short lag because weekday footfall is restored before discretionary shopping normalizes.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by at least 10 points week-on-week after a prior weekly trough
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell to -43.3 at t-1w then rebounded to -14.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES rebounds but RETAIL_REC stays below the last-4-week mean for the next 28 days, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained shift toward staying home suppresses impulse retail trips, so higher RESIDENTIAL mobility should precede lower retail-and-recreation mobility over the next one to two weeks. This effect is strongest when RESIDENTIAL stays above its prior-week level while WORKPLACES remains depressed.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed positive at 7.0 in t-0w while WORKPLACES remained negative at -14.0
failure_condition: If weeks with higher RESIDENTIAL do not coincide with lower RETAIL_REC within 14 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp collapse in TRANSIT indicates a mobility restriction or avoidance shock that reduces access to shopping districts and lowers RETAIL_REC over the following month. The mechanism should appear after TRANSIT drops below its recent average and remain visible until transit partially normalizes.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -25 after being above -20 in the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -33.3 at t-1w to -21.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: If a transit drop below -25 is followed by flat or rising RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS mobility signals warmer-weather leisure activity and broader out-of-home movement, which spills into shopping trips over the next four weeks. When PARKS rises sharply from a prior low, RETAIL_REC should follow upward as discretionary outing intensity increases.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 15 points week-on-week from a depressed level
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -35.0 at t-2w to -14.6 at t-1w before falling again to -36.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS rebounds but RETAIL_REC does not rise above its prior 4-week mean within 28 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A synchronized rise in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES increases city-center circulation and lunch-time shopping opportunities, pushing retail visits higher within one week. The effect requires both commuting proxies to improve together; a rise in only one is not enough to move RETAIL_REC materially.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improved at t-0w relative to t-1w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise but RETAIL_REC does not rise in the following week, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM stays elevated relative to its recent baseline, routine errand substitution reduces separate retail-and-recreation trips over the next two weeks. The mechanism predicts lower discretionary shopping because households consolidate outings into essential trips.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above -13 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed near -14 to -12 across the snapshot while RETAIL_REC was volatile
failure_condition: If sustained higher GROCERY_PHARM is followed by no decline in RETAIL_REC within 14 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A short-lived rebound in RETAIL_REC is not durable unless WORKPLACES and TRANSIT also recover. If retail improves while commuting proxies remain weak, the retail lift should reverse within four weeks because it reflects temporary local substitution rather than broad mobility normalization.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC rises by at least 5 points in one week while WORKPLACES stays below -20
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose at t-1w but fell sharply again at t-0w
failure_condition: If a retail uptick occurs alongside weak WORKPLACES and weak TRANSIT but persists or accelerates for 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A broad decline in PARKS combined with weaker TRANSIT signals weather- or season-driven indoor substitution that lowers discretionary retail trips over the next four weeks. The effect should appear when outdoor leisure and city circulation both retreat at the same time.
candidate_trigger: PARKS and TRANSIT both fall by at least 10 points from the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS and TRANSIT were both weak at multiple points in the snapshot
failure_condition: If simultaneous declines in PARKS and TRANSIT are not followed by lower RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days, the hypothesis fails.
